correctness.rationale: Vergara's normalized parameter x is t/(q+1), and the radial polynomials span the polynomials, so the representing measure is unique even among signed finite measures. As an independent check on the reference law, pruning the root gives the branch resolvent h=1/(z−qh) with h∼1/z; the root resolvent is 1/(z−(q+1)h). Its upper half-plane boundary values give the displayed Kesten density on [−2√q,2√q], with no pole off this band. For u<1/√q, applying I−uA+qu²I to the ℓ² geometric column gives (1−u²)δ, so the density is F_u=(1−u²)/(1+qu²−ut). At the critical u, domination by a constant times (2√q−t)^(−1/2) relative to dt near the upper edge excludes an atom. For u>1/√q, the reciprocally paired scale v=1/(qu) is subcritical and F_u=B_uF_v; the common spherical recurrence and the values at n=0,1 give the remaining positive atom C_u δ_(u⁻¹+qu). For s above critical, its atom is unmatched because u⁻¹+qu is strictly increasing above critical; at critical the ratio F_r/F_s tends to zero. Both force λ=0. Below critical, positivity is exactly the lower bound of F_r/F_s on the band. The ratio derivative has sign (r−s)(1−qrs), giving the specified edge or constant case and the endpoint convention at r=1/√q. Away from collapse the density is positive almost everywhere, and the finite quadratic form against the reference measure is Σ|c_i|², establishing strictness. At collapse the frozen result does not claim strictness; indeed the vector supported on a vertex and its full neighbor set, with coefficients −t_r at the vertex and 1 on each neighbor, is a null vector by the spherical eigenfunction identity. The uploaded script was inspected, not executed.

evidence: Vergara gives both an operator test and a radial positive-measure criterion for all radial kernels. Haagerup–Knudby give the unique spherical measure on finite-rank free groups; their framework includes even-degree trees. Picardello studies spherical representations in a more general tree setting.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These are general criteria, not two-profile comparisons. Even the explicit operator test gives an infinite positivity problem when the two sequences are substituted; a reduction and evaluation are needed to produce the scalar threshold and switch. In the spectral approach the non-ℓ² geometric profile cannot be handled by continuing the density alone, since it acquires an out-of-band atom.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the complete sharp scalar domination cone for distinct geometric scales on regular trees, including the obstruction at and above the smaller critical scale and the change of limiting frequency. The collapsed kernel's identity as a two-exponential spherical function is a direct specialization of a classical formula and is not independent novelty. The inspected prior formulas do not themselves evaluate the full two-scale order: beyond identifying that spherical function, one needs the distinct-scale representing densities, their edge behavior and comparison, and the unmatched-atom obstruction. Priority is best-of-knowledge only.

value.rationale: For a natural family of stationary radial covariance candidates, the exact domination weight over arbitrary finite site sets is needed to know when a smaller-range component can be subtracted. The complete threshold determines a qualitative obstruction not visible in finite numerical Gram tests and exposes when either spectral edge or an unmatched atom is decisive. That value is in the closed classification, not in recasting the known spherical eigenfunction identity.
